title: The Loudest Sound
subtitle: Krakatoa, 27 August 1883
facts_note: Sources: Royal Society, The Eruption of Krakatoa and Subsequent Phenomena (1888); Smithsonian GVP; USGS. The 1888 report is careful: sound 'certainly' at Ceylon (~2,000 mi) and 'probably' at Rodrigues (~3,000 mi, 4,830 km) - the film says what the harbour master heard, and calls it nearly 3,000 miles. There is no reliable decibel figure: the nearest gauge was driven off its chart, and 194 dB is the ceiling for a sound wave in air, so popular '310 dB' numbers are not used here.

lines.text: On the 27th of August, 1883, an island in the Sunda Strait began to come apart.
lines.spoken: On the twenty seventh of August, eighteen eighty three, an island in the Sunda Strait began to come apart.
lines.hero: the strait map: the island in the channel between Java and Sumatra

lines.text: The third blast, at 10:02 that morning, is the loudest sound in recorded history.
lines.spoken: The third blast, at two minutes past ten that morning, is the loudest sound in recorded history.
lines.hero: 1883 lithograph of the column, and the time

lines.text: Forty miles away, the pressure broke men's eardrums.
lines.spoken: Forty miles away, the pressure broke men's eardrums.
lines.hero: distance ring at 40 miles, ship Norham Castle

lines.text: A hundred miles off, at Batavia, a gasometer jumped off its trace.
lines.spoken: A hundred miles off, at Batavia, a gasometer jumped off its trace.
lines.hero: Batavia on the map, the barograph card

lines.text: Inside the strait, it did not arrive as sound at all. It arrived as a wall of air.
lines.spoken: Inside the strait, it did not arrive as sound at all. It arrived as a wall of air.
lines.hero: the shock ring crossing the strait, ships

lines.text: Then the sea came.
lines.spoken: Then the sea came.
lines.hero: the strait map, the coastlines

lines.text: Waves ran a hundred feet high into the towns of the strait.
lines.spoken: Waves ran a hundred feet high into the towns of the strait.
lines.hero: wave height bar against houses

lines.text: 36,417 people died. Most of them were drowned, not burned.
lines.spoken: Thirty six thousand four hundred and seventeen people died. Most of them were drowned, not burned.
lines.hero: the counter, over the Java coast

lines.text: On Sebesi, eight miles away, three thousand people lived. None survived.
lines.spoken: On Sebesi, eight miles away, three thousand people lived. None survived.
lines.hero: Sebesi island, crossed out

lines.text: Two thirds of the island fell into the sea, and left a caldera.
lines.spoken: Two thirds of the island fell into the sea, and left a caldera.
lines.hero: the before/after island outline

lines.text: A Dutch gunboat, the Berouw, was carried two miles inland.
lines.spoken: A Dutch gunboat, the Berouw, was carried two miles inland.
lines.hero: the inland arrow, the wreck card

lines.text: Nearly three thousand miles away, a harbour master heard what he took for heavy guns.
lines.spoken: Nearly three thousand miles away, a harbour master heard what he took for heavy guns.
lines.hero: Rodrigues on the ring sheet, 4,830 km

lines.text: The air wave kept going. Barographs in London and Washington picked it up.
lines.spoken: The air wave kept going. Barographs in London and Washington picked it up.
lines.hero: the world map, wave leaves Krakatoa

lines.text: Stations logged it seven times in five days, as it ran round the planet and came back the other way.
lines.spoken: Stations logged it seven times in five days, as it ran round the planet and came back the other way.
lines.hero: the track with seven passes, the ticker

lines.text: The ash went higher, fifty miles up, and the sunsets went red.
lines.spoken: The ash went higher, fifty miles up, and the sunsets went red.
lines.hero: the stratosphere column, the sky turning

lines.text: In London, an artist named William Ashcroft sat on the Thames and sketched them, thousands of times.
lines.spoken: In London, an artist named William Ashcroft sat on the Thames and sketched them, thousands of times.
lines.hero: the Ashcroft plate pinned over London

lines.text: New York sent fire engines to a fire that was the sky.
lines.spoken: New York sent fire engines to a fire that was the sky.
lines.hero: New York, the fire-brigade note

lines.text: The planet cooled by half a degree, and did not warm back for five years.
lines.spoken: The planet cooled by half a degree, and did not warm back for five years.
lines.hero: the temperature ledger

lines.text: Krakatoa was the first disaster the telegraph carried round the world in a day.
lines.spoken: Krakatoa was the first disaster the telegraph carried round the world in a day.
lines.hero: the wire and the dateline

lines.text: And in 1927, out of the same water, Anak Krakatau rose.
lines.spoken: And in nineteen twenty seven, out of the same water, Anak Krakatau rose.
lines.hero: the caldera, the new cone rising

lines.text: The loudest thing we have ever heard was an island, dying.
lines.spoken: The loudest thing we have ever heard was an island, dying.
lines.hero: the pull-back: the whole sheet
